newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOTTOM SEEN ON SLIDING BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BOTTOM SEEN ON SLIDING BOURSE.

text.p: *Lithuanian dealers were in a bearish mood on Thursday as the Vilnius bourse nose dived but some said that prices seemed to have bottomed out.
*Overall market volume was around 5.8 million litas with secondary T-bills accounting for the lion's share in trade of 5.26 million litas.
*The central market turned over a dull 540,000 litas.
*The Litin A index shed 158.89 points, falling to 2,219.55.
*The official index inched down 3.90 points to 934.87.
*Defying the bears, bullish Siauliu Bank shares charged on, gaining significantly for the fourth straight session. It rose almost ten percent to 102.48 litas in trade of 107,000 litas.
Lithuanian dealers were in a bearish mood on Thursday as shares nose dived but some said that there was light at the end of the gloomy tunnel.
Prices have been dropping steadily as investors have chosen to sit on the sidelines in the hope of buying at bargain prices.
Investors, especially foreign buyers, have also recently shown a preference for the local government debt market over equity markets, dealers said.
But dealers said that this state of affairs had almost run its course and they expected demand for equities to pick up soon.
"Prices seem to have bottomed out...there is room now for an upward correction and prices may begin climbing next week," said Arvydas Jacikevicius of brokerage house Suprema.
He added that over the past few weeks the Estonian bourse seemed to be sucking in much of the foreign money but there were signs that Western investors were seriously examining Lithuania.
A group of senior fund managers visited Lithuania last week to examine the equities market.
Siauliu Bank was one of the few shares to buck the trend, rising steeply for the fourth straight session, gaining to 102.48 litas from 93.17 litas in relatively high trade of 107,000 litas.
Dealers said the bank's price is being fueled by Hermis Bank's intention to acquire a majority stake in it.
